summary: @or-sdk/keys preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated 727KB bundle
details: package.json declares preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is an obfuscated dropper (hex-mangled identifiers such as _0x488df8/_0x52943e, per-function lookup objects mapping opaque keys to strings like "ldd", "/etc/os-release", "Alpine", "bun") that downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<V>/<archive>.zip (or reuses a `bun` on PATH), makes it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js in the package directory via execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js], {cwd}). math_init.js is a 727KB obfuscator.io-style Bun-CJS bundle (banner `// @bun @bun-cjs`, rotated string array, custom-alphabet decoder function hc1jfK9, hex-named variables). The bundle is not part of the package's advertised Keys SDK API in dist/ and is reachable only through the preinstall path; because it runs under Bun rather than Node, Node-based scanners never observe its execution. Fetching an alternate runtime from an official vendor domain would normally be aggressive-but-legitimate, but here the runtime is the vehicle for executing an obfuscated, purpose-mismatched, package-shipped payload at install time, which is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
